description: As the Wayfinders, we want to find solutions to a variety of problems. We express interest in helping people, researching, Earth Science, writing, and creating. With these in mind, we want to create something to solve the problem we are faced with in the challenge.
summary:
Sibol is a website created to support Filipino farmers’, especially farmers from Laguna, continued growth and development amidst unpredictable conditions. We live in a world where climate change has become a pressing issue, making temperatures and weather shift rapidly. As climate change continues to worsen, agriculture will be one of the first industries to be affected.

To combat this, farmers carefully select crops and rotate them accordingly to make their harvest more resilient against these extreme conditions. Sibol was made to aid farmers in making decisions about these crop rotations, using data available online from resources such as NASA and the Philippines’ Department of Agriculture. Farmers may input their current area in Laguna as well as their most previously planted crop to receive a field analysis and recommendations for the next crop rotation.

Sibol was also created in line with the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals: Zero Hunger (SDG 2), Life on Land (SDG 15), and Climate Action (SDG 13).
details:
CONTEXT

The Philippines has always been prone to natural disasters and harsh weather conditions due to its geography. Located near the Equator, it is often hit directly by typhoons and droughts. As an archipelago with many coastal areas and riverside communities, flooding is also a frequent phenomenon in the country. As climate change continues to worsen, the Philippines is one of the first countries who experience the worst of its effects.

Our team Wayfinders has witnessed this firsthand, especially in our home province of Laguna. Laguna has been identified to be one of the most vulnerable provinces when it comes to climate change (Arias et.al, 2016). Home to Laguna de Bay and many other river systems and bodies of water, flooding is also a common occurrence in many municipalities. At the same time, temperatures continue to rise. All of these factors combine together to create a significant problem for Filipino farmers, especially those who reside in Laguna.

Sibol aims to help Lagunense farmers make more informed decisions for their crop rotations by providing accessible NASA and government data on current meteorological events. 

HOW IT WORKS

When farmers input their Laguna municipality via the dropdown menu, they will receive a field analysis. This analysis shows them the current weather in their area as well as a forecast using data from the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA). They are also shown the history of weather conditions in their area, such as the typical amount of rainfall per month. It also provides other helpful information such as El Niño outlooks and soil wetness using not only PAGASA but also NASA POWER and the USA NOAA. It also warns farmers of the geological conditions in their specific municipality that may make them more prone to certain meteorological events such as flooding, and also informs them how weather conditions can make their crops more prone to disease or pests. This information helps them make decisions about what crops are best suited to their current weather conditions, and helps them be aware of the risks that come along with it.

Farmers can also input their current crop details. They can input the current crop they’re planting, the kind of soil, harvest date, and other relevant information. Afterwards, Sibol will give a recommendation on what crop they can plant next to avoid pests and diseases and also maintain soil quality. This recommendation is based on expert data, research, and advisories from the Department of Agriculture and the University of the Philippines Los Baños. They are also based on only the most commonly planted crops in Laguna to ensure the recommendation stays relevant. Additionally, the recommendation includes how to properly care for the crop including pests and diseases and other important details like maturity time and different varieties. It is important to note that the recommendation gives information explaining why these crops work and also shows the exact source it based its recommendation on, giving farmers leeway to understand the logic behind the recommendation and read up on the original source to make the decision themselves.

Sibol also links important resources farmers may also use in deciding what crops to plant and rotate. Making decisions about crops requires a lot of information, research, and balancing of trade-offs. Sibol wants to give farmers access to the information they need to make wiser decisions about their crops. 

Embedded into the site is a satellite view of the farmers’ selected municipality. Using NASA GIBS layers, farmers are able to see conditions such as crop greenness, rainfall rate, and daytime ground heat. There is also a pop-up that explains the usage, view and importance of each GIBS layer. Direct links to relevant government agencies they may reach out to like the Department of Agriculture and the Office of the Provincial Agriculturists are also included. Sites to find more information and advisories related to crop protection are directly linked as well, such as the DA Bureau of Plant Industry and the UPLB National Crop Protection Center. Other NASA sites such as NASA Worldview were included to help farmers with both current and historical meteorological events. Existing apps already frequently used by farmers are also included, namely the DA Geo Camera and RSBSA Finder.

A hyperlink to the Department of Agriculture’s crop price monitoring was also included. Deciding crops is not only a matter of being informed about current weather conditions. Market prices also play a role in farmers deciding which crop to plant next.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

The Philippines is one of the most prone countries to the effects of climate change, and furthermore, Laguna is one of the provinces that suffers heavily due to it. This issue is even further exacerbated by the fact that the agriculture sector plays a major role in the country’s economy. Sibol was created with the intention of providing support to Lagunense farmers as they continue to face harsh and unpredictable conditions. This site aims to help educate farmers on how to combat this issue and aims to give them the tools they need to be more resilient and well-informed with the decisions they make in their livelihoods. 

Additionally, the majority of Laguna’s farmers are of older age (most farmers are 50-70 years old). Most of them find it difficult to adapt to and keep track of the many different advancements in technology as time passes. Sibol was designed to be a central hub for all relevant resources and apps farmers may need to aid them in their livelihoods, and makes accessing different information and tools more streamlined and organized. Sibol also allows them to explore new apps that would benefit their farming experience. 

It is also important to note that there are links to government agencies that could help farmers in a multitude of ways, such as how the Department of Agriculture CALABARZON (DA-CALABARZON) helps farmers stay updated about relevant agricultural news, the Department of Agriculture - Agricultural Training Institute (DA-ATI) teaches new farming techniques and skills, the Office of the Provincial Agriculturists (FAES) for Laguna can be turned to for any concerns regarding farming and are mainly in charge of implementing new projects for agriculture, the RSBSA Finder app allows farmers to find their register and apply for government support, and the DA GeoCamera helps record crop activities which can be used in future reports.

The main benefit of familiarizing oneself with the Department of Agriculture - Bureau of Plant Industry (DA-BPI) and UPLB National Crop Protection Centers is that they give out information on how to control pests in farms, including treatment of the crops to remove pests, which can benefit the growth and harvesting season of the crops.

HOW IT WAS DEVELOPED

We originally drafted our website in Canva and Google Docs, and after finalizing the details we coded our website in HTML using Visual Studio Code. Claude SI was used in the programming, debugging, and troubleshooting our website. While the UI design and information was inputted in the code by the team. Our project is creative both in function and design, as our website is both aesthetically pleasing, having a fitting color palette that is not too hard on the eyes, and functionally easy to understand, featuring a tutorial that easily shows new users how it functions and provides clear and accessible data. Our team had to consider a number of factors, including how well versed farmers would be with technology, as many farmers are older and not experienced with how new websites would work. This became a key factor to consider in designing our website, hence our implementation of an easy UI to follow and tutorial section to guide first time users and help them familiarize themselves with the website.

There are additional pop-up informations to clarify and explain the usage of each tool in the website, especially the GIBS layers and tour around the website. Most of the references that discuss how to plant and produce the crops such as corn, eggplant and pumpkin were the data used in the recommendation. Other references were also used to describe the current temperature, weather, humidity, advisory on the El Niño and images used in the website.
